# Conclusion {#sec-conclusion}

RQ1 asked whether delegation varies with stakes, over time, with error costs and across countries (@sec-rq1, @tbl-rq1-confirmatory-table). H1 is {{< var rq1.h1.decision_text >}}: the null that the education or the wage coefficient is zero is not rejected at {{< var rq1.holm.h1 >}}, with an H1 p-value of {{< var rq1.h1.p >}} and $\beta_e$ = {{< var rq1.h1.beta_e >}} pp of automation per year of education ({{< var rq1.h1.human_education_years_mean.ci_low >}} to {{< var rq1.h1.human_education_years_mean.ci_high >}}); $\beta_w$ is opposite in sign to H1's prediction and is not significant at its Holm level. R24 r5 is the one robustness row under which that p-value ({{< var rob.r24.r5.p_h1.p >}}) falls below that level with both coefficients negative, and it changes no decision. H2 is {{< var rq1.h2.decision_text >}}: the release-level co-condition fails, with task-clustered p {{< var rq1.h2.p_cluster >}} beside wild-bootstrap p = {{< var rq1.h2.p_wild >}} at {{< var rq1.holm.h2 >}}. The measured rise is one r2-to-r3 step followed by a fall, leaving out r2 reverses the sign of β ({{< var diag.h2.leave_out_release_r2.beta >}} pp per year; post-result diagnostic, PAP §11 D-3; exploratory; not a decision; @tbl-diag-h2-influence), and the step coincides with a change of the classified-conversation base, so classifier or platform drift cannot be separated from behaviour; R22 `api_r3_r5` and R23 run the other way. The balanced panel removes {{< var diag.h2.balancing_removed.n_tasks >}} tasks holding {{< var diag.h2.balancing_removed.usage_share_pct >}} per cent of usage (descriptive). H3 is {{< var rq1.h3.decision_text >}}: the null that γ is zero is not rejected at {{< var rq1.holm.h3 >}}, with γ = {{< var rq1.h3.gamma >}} pp of validation share ({{< var rq1.h3.error_cost.ci_low >}} to {{< var rq1.h3.error_cost.ci_high >}}; p = {{< var rq1.h3.error_cost.p >}}). H4 is {{< var rq1.h4.decision_text >}}: the joint Wald test rejects at {{< var rq1.holm.h4 >}} (p {{< var rq1.h4.p_wald >}}), with b₁ = {{< var rq1.h4.b1 >}} pp per unit of log AUI and b₂ = {{< var rq1.h4.b2 >}} pp per unit of log GDP per working-age person, a unit of a log being a hundred log points. The two regressors are strongly correlated across countries, so each coefficient is weakly separable on its own, although the joint test is not.

RQ2 is descriptive (@sec-rq2). Across the {{< var design.n_industries >}} industries, delegation exposure's Spearman correlation with the human-rated Eloundou benchmark is {{< var rq2.b.z_delegation.z_eloundou.rho >}} (interval {{< var rq2.b.z_delegation.z_eloundou.ci.lo >}} to {{< var rq2.b.z_delegation.z_eloundou.ci.hi >}}) (@tbl-rq2-could-vs-does-b). "Could" and "does" order the industries similarly, with qualifications. Both sides share the same OEWS occupation-to-industry weights, so part of the correlation is common occupational mix; and the correlation depends on the D3 assumption that occupations unpublished in AEI carry zero usage, which R3 relaxes, lowering it most ({{< var rob.r03.spearman_z_eloundou_vs_z_delegation.estimate >}}; @sec-app-robustness-tables). Design B is out of sample in AEI data only: its {{< var vintage.oews.primary >}} OEWS weights were released on {{< var design.s1.oews_release >}}, after the {{< var design.formation >}} formation date and inside the return window, and its O\*NET {{< var vintage.onet.primary >}} links postdate formation, so it is not strictly real-time; R32 is market-only.

For RQ3 the D11 rule fires: the primary MDE of {{< var d11.primary_mde >}} pp per standard deviation exceeds the plausibility threshold of {{< var design.plausibility_pp >}} pp, a threshold confirmed with the MDE in view, so the market evidence is reported as what it can and cannot yet say (@sec-markets). Over the {{< var design.window.months >}}-month window the results read, in their fixed wording (@tbl-rq3-confirmatory): {{< var rq3.h5.wording >}} {{< var rq3.h5b.wording >}} The two decisions (H5 {{< var rq3.h5.decision_text >}}, H5b {{< var rq3.h5b.decision_text >}}) rest on the Design B inputs whose timing is stated above. Under the strict real-time inputs of R32 ({{< var vintage.oews.r32 >}} weights), the H5 and H5b slopes are {{< var rob.r32.h5.estimate >}} and {{< var rob.r32.h5b.estimate >}} pp (@sec-app-robustness-tables); R1 is look-ahead. Neither non-rejection says that exposure is unrelated to returns. Each says that this window could detect only a departure from the historical pattern at least as large as its MDE.

Only a more powerful test, not another reading of this one, could change the market conclusion. Under the pre-registered test the MDE is {{< var power.mde_over_s >}} times s, the across-window spread of the historical slopes ({{< var power.s.h5 >}} pp for H5, {{< var power.s.h5b >}} pp for H5b), so a future window would lead the paper with RQ3 only if its own s brought the MDE, here {{< var rq3.h5.mde >}} and {{< var rq3.h5b.mde >}} pp, to the {{< var design.plausibility_pp >}} pp threshold or below. Because R13 is a co-condition of the claim, its MDEs, {{< var rq3.h5.mde_r13 >}} pp and {{< var rq3.h5b.mde_r13 >}} pp, would have to fall as well. Until such a window exists, the evidence on how the model is used rests on RQ1 and RQ2.
